subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the value of k if the angle between the straight lines 4x−y+7=0, kx−5y−9=0 is 45°.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.62 — SAQ chapter 9 The Straight Line, answer 57. Printed appearances: TS M-17 · AP M-16. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed against this answer. It is not a bare guess: the SAME CHAPTER prints 1+1+2 on answer 59 (book p.63), and this answer is cut to the same shape — the two setting-up moves at one mark each and the closing work at two. Where an answer's own shape is four equal moves instead, 1+1+1+1 is used and this note says so. Paper position: Maths-1B Section B runs Q11-Q17 at 4 marks each, answer any 5 of 7. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. NOTE: The Straight Line is the FIRST Maths-1B unit to occupy ALL THREE sections of the paper — the book's IPE Blue Print (book p.3) gives it 2+2 marks in Section A, 4 in Section B and 7 in Section C, 15 in all, tying Differentiation as the highest-scoring unit on the paper. It therefore has three separate chapters in this book: LAQ chapter 1 (book pp.14-18), SAQ chapter 9 (pp.61-64) and VSAQ chapter 14 (pp.79-82). recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — name the angle formula, and say why this question has two answers.

steps.label: Both slopes
steps.margin_note: First mark. Read both slopes off the coefficients as −a/b. The second carries the unknown, which is exactly what the angle condition will pin down.
steps.memory_tip: Read both slopes off the coefficients as −a/b; the second carries the unknown.
lines: Given line is 4x − y + 7 = 0.  It's slope  m₁ = −a/b = −4/(−1) = 4
Another line is kx − 5y − 9 = 0.  It's slope  m₂ = −a/b = −k/(−5) = k/5

recall.must_convey: That m₁ = 4 and m₂ = k/5 are read off the coefficients.
accept: the slopes are four and k over five
read both slopes as minus a over b
m one is four and m two is k by five
rendu slopes minus a by b tho teesukovali
both slopes first

steps.why: Both slopes are needed before the angle formula can be written, and one of them carrying the unknown is what makes this solvable.
common_mistakes: Reading the slope of 4x − y + 7 = 0 as −4 by forgetting the sign of b.

steps.label: Write the angle formula
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The angle between two lines is tanθ = |(m₁ − m₂)/(1 + m₁m₂)|. At 45° the tangent is 1, so the whole modulus equals 1.
steps.memory_tip: tan θ = |(m₁ − m₂)/(1 + m₁m₂)|, and at 45° the tangent is 1, so the modulus equals 1.
lines: Angle between the lines is 45°, then

recall.must_convey: That tanθ = |(m₁ − m₂)/(1 + m₁m₂)| is written and tan45° = 1 is used.
accept: tan theta is mod of m one minus m two over one plus m one m two
write the angle formula and put tan forty five equals one
the angle formula between two lines
angle formula rasi tan forty five equals one pettali
use the tangent of the angle between two lines
heard_as: one plus m one m two

steps.why: tan45° = 1 is what turns an angle condition into a plain algebraic equation.
common_mistakes: Using sinθ or cosθ instead of tanθ.

steps.label: Open the modulus
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Clear the fractions inside first, then remove the modulus as PLUS OR MINUS — that ± is why this question has two answers rather than one.
steps.memory_tip: Clear the fractions inside FIRST, then open the modulus as ±. That ± is why there are two answers.

recall.must_convey: That clearing the fractions gives |5 + 4k| = |20 − k|, which opens as ±.
accept: clear the fractions then remove the mod as plus or minus
five plus four k equals plus or minus twenty minus k
the modulus gives two cases
mod theeste plus or minus rendu cases vasthaayi
open the modulus both ways

steps.why: An angle of 45° can be measured to either line, so both branches are genuine answers — dropping one loses half the marks.
common_mistakes: Dropping the ± and finding only one value of k.
Multiplying out the fractions incorrectly and losing the 5.

steps.label: Solve both branches
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Solve each branch separately and report both values.
steps.memory_tip: Solve each branch separately and report BOTH values.

recall.must_convey: That the two branches give k = 3 and k = −25/3.
accept: solve both cases to get k equals three and k equals minus twenty five by three
the two branches give two values of k
k is three or minus twenty five over three
rendu cases solve chesthe rendu values vasthaayi
both values of k

steps.why: Two lines through a point make two pairs of angles, 45° and 135°, and both satisfy the modulus equation — so two values of k are expected, not a sign of error.
common_mistakes: Sign slip when distributing the minus over (20 − k).

insider_note: tan45° = 1 turns the formula into |5 + 4k| = |20 − k|, so the modulus opens into TWO equations. Both k = 3 and k = −25/3 are answers; stopping at the whole number loses the last mark.
